claims.text: The feedstock is pre-alloyed AlCrFeNiSi powder prepared for additive manufacturing.
An in-situ annealing dwell at or below 700 °C between PBF-LB laser passes will reduce residual thermal stress in AlCrFeNiSi components.
The in-situ annealing step will refine the microstructure of AlCrFeNiSi components.
The in-situ annealing step will improve mechanical properties relative to conventional high-thermal-load processing.
The proposed processing window uses a PBF-LB layer thickness of 20–50 µm.
The build should be maintained at or below 700 °C through an interlayer dwell.
The intervention is applicable to miniature, thin-walled AlCrFeNiSi structures.
Performance should be evaluated under both ambient and cryogenic conditions.
Temporary low-temperature annealing reduces dislocation density.
Temporary low-temperature annealing mitigates grain-size variation across the build height.
Residual-stress relief occurs through limited diffusion and dislocation rearrangement.
Annealing at or below 700 °C can relieve stress without triggering full recrystallization.
The intervention will produce a more uniform microstructure while preserving mechanical integrity.
Annealed components will have a more homogeneous microstructure with refined grains.
Annealed components will exhibit enhanced ductility.
Annealed components will retain yield strength comparable to or greater than conventionally processed controls.
Conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing commonly causes internal or residual stress buildup.

Additively manufactured thin-walled structures can exhibit build-height-dependent grain size, dislocation density, and mechanical properties because of thermal-gradient and heat-accumulation differences.
The intervention's effectiveness for larger builds and other alloy systems is undetermined.
The optimal dwell duration, precise temperature control, scalability, and throughput impact remain uncertain.
